turn_text: Well, the Federal Reserve yesterday raised interest rates. I think it's the largest jump in interest rates in nearly 40 years. I think that they were right to take a bold step. Inflation is really dogging Minnesotans, especially increases in prices for food and gas and fuel. Of course, raising the interest rates at the Federal Reserve doesn't have a direct impact on lowering food prices. But what it does do is sort of cool the overall economy. I know that what the Federal Reserve is trying to do is to kind of slow down the economy without pushing us into a recession because of course what we don't want is to have people start to lose their jobs because companies start to cut back and that would also be bad. But I think that they do have a very important lever with interest rates to address some of the challenges of inflation. Of course, inflation is being driven in large part by all of these supply chain problems by the war in Ukraine by fuel prices because the Saudi folks haven't been increasing the production of oil. And so that's been driving up oil prices.
